That wedding day, with the tall, slender, dark-haired, blue-eyed Wallis in a gown of white panne velvet, made with a "court" train, wearing a veil of tulle and carrying white orchids, must have seemed a story-book ending for the girl who, until then, had had little, indeed, of the world's good things.

She was the daughter of a clerk and of a young wife who had beauty, impressive family connections—and practically no money.

Before her third birthday, Bessie Wallis was fatherless.

She grew up in the boarding house operated by her mother; operated genteelly, but still a boarding house.

As a young girl, she knew, if not poverty, the distinctly unpleasant status of a "poor relation" and the persistence of bill collectors.

Bessie Wallis Warfield married E. Winfield Spencer, Jr., in fashionable Christ Episcopal Church, amid palms and white chrysanthemums and before a candle-lighted altar, but the young couple did not "live happily ever after."

Instead, the bride was destined to be labelled, legally, a "deserted wife."

She was to pass through the divorce courts, to know the scourge of gossiping tongues.

She was, later, to remarry, to enter the gayest, most brilliant social circles of London, Paris, Biarritz, Cannes and St. Moritz, to be seen more and more frequently in the presence of royalty and, within the last few weeks, to blossom forth as the most talked-of woman in the world.

An amazing story . . . more unbelievable, more fantastic than an ancient Horatio Alger epic entitled, "From Rags to Riches," is the present-day, real life drama of newspaper headlines, photographs and European statecraft. "From Boarding House to Balmoral."

It all began 40 years ago—
The T. Wallis Warfields' daughter, a first and only child, was born at the home of her paternal grandmother, Mrs. Henry M. Warfield, in Baltimore.

The parents—particularly the father—had wanted a boy. Refusing to sacrifice completely his dreams of a son to carry on his name, T. Wallis Warfield decided the baby should be named "Wallis" for himself and "Bessie" for her aunt, Mrs. D. Buchanan Merryman of Washington, nee Bessie Montague.

The child was so christened and, from that day to this, Bessie Wallis Simpson has had no stauncher, closer friend than Mrs. Merryman.

It was she who accompanied her niece on her first trip to Europe, it was she who comforted Wallis after the death of her mother in 1929. It was Mrs. Merryman who chaperoned Mrs. Simpson on many of the European holiday trips when she was among the guests of His Royal Highness, the Prince of Wales, now King Edward VIII of England.

Today Mrs. Merryman scouts rumors that Mr. and Mrs. Simpson are contemplating divorce, is "distressed" by newspaper novelty attending her niece's recent visit at Balmoral Castle and her presence with other guests, on the royal yacht Nahlin on the King's recent Mediterranean holiday.

"The talk of divorce," Mrs. Merryman told me, "is nothing whatever but gossip, invented and spread by people who delight in scandal. It is simply not true. I feel that I cannot stand to see another of it—so unjust, so unkind—untrue!"

Merryman's attitude of concern is quite in contrast with that of famous Mrs. Simpson herself when a fellow townsman of hers called on her in London summer.

"How are you?" Mrs. Simpson asked pleasantly.

"Right, Wallis. You're doing well, too, aren't you?"

"Yes," Mrs. Simpson laughed. "I think I've done badly at 'o you?"

ally likes to hear from her friends and is always cordial. Another of them, in a telephone conversation one day last summer, recalled occasions when one of chief concerns was a certain department store's bills.

"I think," she said, "that perhaps if I went back to Baltimore ———'s store might GIVE me a pair of shoes, don't you?"

Far cry from shoe bills it is! The current report that Londoners already are at work on a dress made of 18 silver fox skins, extremely rare quality and extremely high price which Mrs. Simpson will wear at the coronation ceremonies next year.

The King's deep friendship for boarding house keeper's daughter is attested by a Baltimore man who has known Mrs. Simpson since childhood, met her at Biarritz a year ago and had tea with her. King Edward VIII, then Prince of Wales, also was present.

Whenever Wallis speaks," says a traveler, "he seems to be sim enthralled. He hangs on every word she says, roars at anything it is amusing—and Wallis is y amusing. His eyes and manner give the impression that there is no one else in the room."

These close friends who know Wallis Simpson well, who have visited her London apartment, dined with her at Cannes and in Switzerland, take no stock whatever in rumors that Ernest Simpson will seek to sever the bonds of his marriage.

On the contrary, they insist that His Majesty, Edward VIII, has a friendship for Simpson and that, as a measure of this esteem, they look to see the American knighted.

"That," pointed out one of Wallis's friends, with a toss of her head, "would make her Lady Simpson!"

Carter G. Osburn, a beau of her school days who now is selling automobiles, considers this prospect, smiling.

"Wallis wasn't socially ambitious when she was a girl," he says. "She was too independent for that. But I think she is superbly fitted for a career as an international hostess—clever, tactful, sympathetic. Of course, I always thought she was about perfect, and I'm sure she has become a completely charming woman."

Another loyal friend of Wallis Simpson is Mrs. John Sadler of Cockeysville, Md., the former Emily McLane Merryman. Distantly related, they went to Arundel school together. Mrs. Sadler made her bow in society the same night as Mrs. Simpson. She was one of the bridesmaids when Wallis married her first husband, Earl Winfield Spencer, Jr.

Proudly Mrs. Sadler displays the slender gold bracelet on her wrist—one of those the bride gave to each of her six bridesmaids.

"I haven't seen Wallis in years," Mrs. Sadler says, "but we've always been friends and I've always admired her.

"As long as I live I'll never forget the dress she wore the night of the Bachelor's Cotillion, the night we were presented. It was white satin with an overskirt of chiffon and wide bands of pearl embroidery around the bottom. The rest of us wore simple little things, but Wallis's dress was really stunning.

"I certainly wish I still had my bridesmaid's dress. Wallis designed her wedding gown and our dresses, too. She always wore clothes well and she had a lovely figure."

As for beauty, Dr. Frederic Taylor, a friend of the family for years, says, "All of her features are good, yet, put together, they do not make beauty. The effect is rather that of a sparkling personality and good nature—more intriguing than beauty. Wallis is like her mother in this respect."

TOMORROW: Wallis Warfield's debutante days.

在那个婚礼之日，身材高挑、纤细、黑发蓝眼的华莉丝（Wallis）身着白色平绒礼服，拖着“宫廷式”长后摆，头戴薄纱面纱，手捧白色兰花，对于此前几乎未曾享有多少世间福泽的她来说，这场景想必如同童话故事般圆满。

她是一名职员的女儿，母亲年轻貌美，家族背景显赫——但 practically 没有钱财。

贝茜·华莉丝（Bessie Wallis）未满三岁便失去了父亲。

她在母亲经营的寄宿公寓中长大；虽然经营得体面，但终究是一家寄宿公寓。

少女时期的她，即便未陷于赤贫，也深知身为“穷亲戚”那种令人极不愉快的地位，以及讨债人 incessant 的纠缠。

贝茜·华莉丝·沃菲尔德（Bessie Wallis Warfield）在时尚基督圣公会教堂（Christ Episcopal Church）嫁给了小厄尔·温菲尔德·斯宾塞（E. Winfield Spencer, Jr.），婚礼现场棕榈环绕，白菊簇拥，祭坛烛光摇曳，但这对年轻夫妇并未从此“幸福地生活在一起”。

相反，新娘注定要在法律上被贴上“被遗弃的妻子”的标签。

她将经历离婚法庭的审判，饱受流言蜚语的折磨。

后来，她再婚，跻身伦敦、巴黎、比亚里茨（Biarritz）、戛纳和圣莫里茨最欢快、最耀眼的社交圈，越来越频繁地出现在王室成员面前，并在最近几周内，成为举世议论最多的女性。

一个惊人的故事……比古老的霍雷肖·阿尔杰（Horatio Alger）史诗《从衣衫褴褛到腰缠万贯》更令人难以置信、更离奇的是，这是由报纸头条、照片和欧洲政治权谋构成的当代现实戏剧。“从寄宿公寓到巴尔莫勒尔堡。”

一切始于40年前——
T. 华莉丝·沃菲尔德（T. Wallis Warfield）的女儿，也是独生女，出生于巴尔的摩其 paternal 祖母亨利·M. 沃菲尔德夫人（Mrs. Henry M. Warfield）的家中。

父母——尤其是父亲——原本想要一个男孩。T. 华莉丝·沃菲尔德不愿完全放弃让儿子继承香火的梦想，决定给婴儿取名为“华莉丝”以纪念自己，取名为“贝茜”以纪念她的姨妈、华盛顿的 D. 布坎南·梅里曼夫人（Mrs. D. Buchanan Merryman），娘家姓贝茜·蒙塔古（Bessie Montague）。

孩子以此受洗，而从那天起至今，贝茜·华莉丝·辛普森再也没有比梅里曼夫人更坚定、更亲密的朋友了。

正是她陪同侄女首次前往欧洲旅行，正是她在1929年华莉丝母亲去世后给予安慰。当辛普森夫人作为威尔士亲王（即现在的英国国王爱德华八世）的宾客在欧洲度假时，也是梅里曼夫人在许多次旅行中担任她的 chaperone（监护人/陪伴者）。

如今，梅里曼夫人驳斥有关辛普森夫妇正考虑离婚的谣言，并对报纸对其侄女近期访问巴尔莫勒尔城堡以及陪同其他宾客登上国王近期地中海假期所用的皇家游艇“纳林号”（Nahlin）的新奇报道感到“苦恼”。

梅里曼夫人告诉我：“关于离婚的说法完全是那些乐于散布丑闻的人编造和传播的流言。这根本不是事实。我觉得我无法忍受再看到这样的报道——如此不公，如此刻薄——不实！”

当一位同乡在夏季拜访伦敦的著名辛普森夫人时，梅里曼夫人的关切态度与辛普森夫人本人的态度形成了鲜明对比。

“你好吗？”辛普森夫人愉快地问道。

“很好，华莉丝。你也过得不错，是吧？”

“是的，”辛普森夫人笑道，“我想我在‘o you?’这件事上做得很糟。”

ally 喜欢收到朋友的来信，且总是热情友好。去年夏天的一次电话交谈中，另一位朋友回忆起当时主要的担忧之一是某家百货公司的账单。

她说：“我想，也许如果我回到巴尔的摩————百货公司可能会送我一双鞋，你不觉得吗？”

这与鞋类账单相去甚远！目前的报道是，伦敦裁缝已经在用18张银狐皮制作一件礼服，这种皮草极其稀有且价格极高，辛普森夫人将在明年的加冕典礼上穿着。

一位自辛普森夫人童年起就认识她、一年前在比亚里茨与她相遇并共进茶点的巴尔的摩男子证实了国王对这位寄宿公寓管理者女儿的深厚友谊。当时的威尔士亲王、现在的爱德华八世国王也在场。

一位旅行者说：“每当华莉丝说话时，他似乎都被迷住了。他仔细聆听她说的每一个字，对任何有趣的事情都开怀大笑——而华莉丝非常风趣。他的眼神和举止给人的印象是房间里没有其他人。”

这些了解华莉丝·辛普森的密友，曾去过她在伦敦的公寓，在戛纳和瑞士与她共进晚餐，他们根本不相信欧内斯特·辛普森（Ernest Simpson）将寻求解除婚姻关系的谣言。

相反，他们坚持认为陛下爱德华八世对辛普森怀有友情，并且作为这种尊重的体现，他们预计这位美国人将被封为爵士。

华莉丝的一位朋友甩着头指出：“那将使她成为辛普森女爵士！”

卡特·G. 奥斯本（Carter G. Osburn），她学生时代的爱慕者，现在从事汽车销售工作，微笑着看待这一前景。

他说：“华莉丝年轻时并没有社交野心。她太独立了，不会那样做。但我认为她非常适合担任国际女主人的职业——聪明、圆滑、富有同情心。当然，我一直认为她近乎完美，我相信她已经成为一个完全迷人的女性。”

华莉丝·辛普森的另一位忠实朋友是马里兰州科基斯维尔（Cockeysville）的约翰·萨德勒夫人（Mrs. John Sadler），即前艾米丽·麦克莱恩·梅里曼（Emily McLane Merryman）。她们有远亲关系，曾一同就读于阿伦德尔学校（Arundel school）。萨德勒夫人与辛普森夫人在同一晚初次亮相社交界。当华莉丝嫁给第一任丈夫小厄尔·温菲尔德·斯宾塞时，她是伴娘之一。

萨德勒夫人自豪地展示手腕上纤细的金手镯——这是新娘送给六位伴娘每人的一件礼物。

萨德勒夫人说：“我多年未见华莉丝，但我们一直是朋友，我一直钦佩她。

只要我活着，我就永远不会忘记我们在单身汉科蒂利翁舞会（Bachelor's Cotillion）那晚穿的衣服，也就是我们初次亮相的那晚。那是白色缎子面料，配有雪纺外裙，底部饰有宽幅珍珠刺绣带。我们其他人穿的都是简单的小礼服，但华莉丝的裙子确实令人惊艳。

我真希望我还保留着我的伴娘礼服。华莉丝设计了她的婚纱和我们的礼服。她穿衣服总是很得体，而且身材很好。”

至于美貌，家族多年的朋友弗雷德里克·泰勒博士（Dr. Frederic Taylor）说：“她的五官都很端正，但组合在一起并不构成传统意义上的美。其效果更像是一种闪耀的个性和好脾气——比美貌更引人入胜。华莉丝在这方面像她的母亲。”

October 19, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

KING OF ENGLAND DOES NOT WISH OTHERS TO INTERFERE WITH HIS
RELATIONS WITH MRS. SIMPSON.

Advice of Political and Religious Leaders Meets
With His Anger.

Will He Give Up His Throne For The Sake Of A Woman?

London, October 17.

According to information from Court
circles to-day, King Edward VIII is angry at the interference
by political and religious leaders with his friendly relations
with Mrs. Simpson, his holiday companion. It is said that
the Archbishop of Canterbury and Mr. Baldwin, the Prime
Minister, recently paid an informal visit to Buckingham
Palace to beseech the King to be discreet about his relations
with Mrs. Simpson. The King was very angry at their inter-
ference with his private affairs, although he did not give
any outward indication of his feelings. His lips trembled
slightly. He requested the Archbishop and the Prime Minister
not to meddle in the affairs of other people.
Mrs. Simpson is the wife of a London
stock broker. It is said that she is seeking a divorce.
However, the people of London seem to be unaware of what
has been going on because nothing about it has been published
in the newspapers. If the affair proves to be well founded,
it will give rise to a violent reaction on the part of the
people. Therefore, the Court officials are very uneasy.
According to information given out by
a certain person connected with the Court, the King recently
received from the people letters criticising the frequent
visits paid by Mrs. Simpson to the Palace. Owing to the
censorship, the Press is unable to publish matters indicating
the King's desire to give up the various traditions of the
Victorian Royal Family. Many rumours are current and it is
possible that the affair will become public in the near
future. (Kuo Min).

London, October 17.

A number of British people to-day believe
that King Edward VIII may abdicate in favour of his brother,
the Duke of York, and retire to the life of a happy country
gentleman. Court circles declare that such a belief is
absolutely groundless, yet the following reasons tend to
lend support to such a belief :-
(1) King Edward VIII does not like the
responsibilities of a King.
(2) He deeply detests interference with
his friendly relations with Mrs. Simpson by leaders of the
religious and conservative parties.
(3) The King has a strong will and it
becomes stronger whenever he is opposed.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

英王不希望他人干涉其与辛普森夫人的关系。

政治和宗教领袖的建议招致其愤怒。

他会为了一个女人放弃王位吗？

伦敦，10月17日。

据今日来自宫廷圈子的消息，爱德华八世国王对政治和宗教领袖干涉他与度假伴侣辛普森夫人的友好关系感到愤怒。据悉，坎特伯雷大主教和首相鲍德温先生最近非正式访问白金汉宫，恳请国王在与辛普森夫人的关系上保持谨慎。国王对他们干涉其私事感到非常愤怒，尽管他没有在外表上流露出任何情绪。他的嘴唇微微颤抖。他请求大主教和首相不要 meddling（干涉）他人的事务。
辛普森夫人是一位伦敦股票经纪人的妻子。据说她正在寻求离婚。然而，伦敦民众似乎对正在发生的事情一无所知，因为报纸上没有刊登任何相关内容。如果此事被证实属实，将引起民众的强烈反应。因此，宫廷官员非常不安。
据一位与宫廷有关的人士透露，国王最近收到民众来信，批评辛普森夫人频繁访问宫殿。由于审查制度，新闻界无法发布表明国王希望放弃维多利亚王室各种传统的消息。谣言四起，此事有可能在不久的将来公之于众。（国民通讯社）。

伦敦，10月17日。

今天，许多英国人认为爱德华八世国王可能会退位，由其弟约克公爵继位，他自己则退隐去过快乐的乡村绅士生活。宫廷圈子宣称这种信念毫无根据，但以下理由倾向于支持这种信念：-
(1) 爱德华八世国王不喜欢国王的责任。
(2) 他深恶痛绝宗教和保守党领袖干涉他与辛普森夫人的友好关系。
(3) 国王意志坚强，且每当受到反对时，其意志会变得更强。

October 19, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Although the newspapers to-day are still reticent over the question of the divorce of the Simpson couple, rumours are very prevalent. The newspaper "Referee" of London to-day publishes on its front page a report entitled "The King may marry next Spring". Recently the Universal Motion Picture Company approached Mrs. Simpson, an intimate friend of the British Crown, to sign a film contract. To-day the company received a telegraphic reply from Mrs. Simpson's secretary stating that Mrs. Simpson is at present not in London and that he cannot give a reply until she comes back to London.

October 19, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

KING OF ENGLAND DOES NOT WISH OTHERS TO INTERFERE WITH HIS
RELATIONS WITH MRS. SIMPSON.

Advice of Political and Religious Leaders Meets
With His Anger.

Will He Give Up His Throne For The Sake Of A Woman?

London, October 17.

According to information from Court
circles to-day, King Edward VIII is angry at the interference
by political and religious leaders with his friendly relations
with Mrs. Simpson, his holiday companion. It is said that
the Archbishop of Canterbury and Mr. Baldwin, the Prime
Minister, recently paid an informal visit to Buckingham
Palace to beseech the King to be discreet about his relations
with Mrs. Simpson. The King was very angry at their inter-
ference with his private affairs, although he did not give
any outward indication of his feelings. His lips trembled
slightly. He requested the Archbishop and the Prime Minister
not to meddle in the affairs of other people.
Mrs. Simpson is the wife of a London
stock broker. It is said that she is seeking a divorce.
However, the people of London seem to be unaware of what
has been going on because nothing about it has been published
in the newspapers. If the affair proves to be well founded,
it will give rise to a violent reaction on the part of the
people. Therefore, the Court officials are very uneasy.
According to information given out by
a certain person connected with the Court, the King recently
received from the people letters criticising the frequent
visits paid by Mrs. Simpson to the Palace. Owing to the
censorship, the Press is unable to publish matters indicating
the King's desire to give up the various traditions of the
Victorian Royal Family. Many rumours are current and it is
possible that the affair will become public in the near
future. (Kuo Min).

London, October 17.

A number of British people to-day believe
that King Edward VIII may abdicate in favour of his brother,
the Duke of York, and retire to the life of a happy country
gentleman. Court circles declare that such a belief is
absolutely groundless, yet the following reasons tend to
lend support to such a belief :-
(1) King Edward VIII does not like the
responsibilities of a King.
(2) He deeply detests interference with
his friendly relations with Mrs. Simpson by leaders of the
religious and conservative parties.
(3) The King has a strong will and it
becomes stronger whenever he is opposed.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

英王不愿他人干涉其与辛普森夫人之关系。

政界及宗教领袖之劝告招致其愤怒。

他会为了一个女人放弃王位吗？

伦敦，10月17日。

据今日来自宫廷圈子的消息，爱德华八世国王对政治和宗教领袖干涉他与度假伴侣辛普森夫人的友好关系感到愤怒。据悉，坎特伯雷大主教和首相鲍德温先生最近非正式访问了白金汉宫，恳请国王在与辛普森夫人的关系上保持谨慎。国王对其私人事务受到干涉感到非常愤怒，尽管他并未在外表上流露出任何情绪。他的嘴唇微微颤抖。他请求大主教和首相不要 meddling（干涉）他人的事务。
辛普森夫人是伦敦一位股票经纪人的妻子。据说她正在寻求离婚。然而，伦敦市民似乎对正在发生的事情一无所知，因为报纸上没有刊登任何相关消息。如果此事被证实确有其事，将会引起民众的强烈反应。因此，宫廷官员们非常不安。
据一位与宫廷有关的人士透露，国王最近收到民众来信，批评辛普森夫人频繁访问王宫。由于审查制度，新闻界无法发布表明国王希望放弃维多利亚王室各种传统的消息。谣言四起，此事有可能在不久的将来公之于众。（《国民》）

伦敦，10月17日。

许多英国人今天认为，爱德华八世国王可能会退位，由其弟约克公爵继位，而他本人则退隐去过幸福的乡绅生活。宫廷圈子宣称这种信念毫无根据，但以下理由倾向于支持这种看法：-
(1) 爱德华八世国王不喜欢国王的责任。
(2) 他深恶痛绝宗教和保守党领袖干涉他与辛普森夫人的友好关系。
(3) 国王意志坚定，且每当受到反对时，其意志变得更加坚强。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 10, 1936

MRS. E. SIMPSON WILL
STAY IN CANNES

Disposal Of Her London
Residence Reason For
"Mystery Hop"

FUTURE INTENTIONS
NOT DISCLOSED

CANNES, Dec. 9.—An announce-
ment of Mrs. Ernest Simpson's in-
tention to remain in Cannes over
Christmas was made last night by
Lord Brownlow, Lord-in-Waiting to
the King, following the arrival in
Marseilles of a "mystery 'plane,"
with three passengers, which had
left Croydon in the morning.

Lord Brownlow stated that Mrs.
Simpson's solicitor, who had arriv-
ed in Marseilles by air, was coming
to Cannes, at his own suggestion,
to discuss details concerning the
disposal of Mrs. Simpson's town
house, as she had "no intention of
returning to London for a consider-
able time."

Mrs. Simpson, he added, was
keeping well.

Much speculation concerning the
identity of the three passengers and
the purpose of their visit to Cannes
was let loose when the "mystery
'plane" bearing them departed from
London.

The machine, whose departure
from Le Bourget, the first stopping-
place, had been delayed for an hour,
proceeded to Lyons, where, after
being refuelled, it departed for
Marseilles.

At Marseilles the three passengers
disembarked, had dinner at a hotel
and left by car at 7.46 p.m. for
Cannes, 90 miles away by road.

It was only then learnt that they
were Mr. Theodore Goddard, Mrs.
Simpson's solicitor, a clerk and Dr.
Kirkwood, a specialist.

Explaining their visit, Lord
Brownlow said that Dr. Kirkwood
was simply a friend of Mr. Goddard,
who was very unwell at the moment
and was unwilling to travel with-
out a doctor.

The passengers, immediately after
their arrival, went to a hotel.—
Reuter.

Dr. Kirkwood Returning

MARSEILLES, Dec. 9.—Dr. Kirk-
wood arrived here to-day on his way
back to England from Cannes.—
Reuter.

E. 辛普森夫人将
留在戛纳

处理其伦敦寓所
是“神秘飞行”之原因

未来意图
未予披露

戛纳，12月9日。— 昨晚，国王侍从长布朗洛勋爵宣布，欧内斯特·辛普森夫人打算在戛纳度过圣诞节。此前，一架载有三名乘客的“神秘飞机”于早晨从克罗伊登起飞，抵达马赛。

布朗洛勋爵表示，辛普森夫人的律师乘飞机抵达马赛后，正按其本人建议前往戛纳，讨论处理辛普森夫人市区住宅的细节，因为她“在相当长的一段时间内无意返回伦敦”。

他补充说，辛普森夫人身体状况良好。

当载有这三名乘客的“神秘飞机”从伦敦起飞时，关于这三名乘客的身份及其访问戛纳的目的引发了诸多猜测。

该飞机在第一站勒布尔歇机场的出发时间延误了一小时，随后飞往里昂，在加油后启程前往马赛。

乘客们抵达后立即前往一家酒店。— 路透社。

SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 10, 1936

KING'S DECISION AWAITED

Abdication Of King Would Be Big Blow

England And Dominions Would Be Plunged In Deep Sadness

PERSONAL LEADERSHIP OF HIS MAJESTY

British Press Confident That Worst Feature Of Crisis Has Passed

LONDON, Dec. 9.—Further comment on the constitutional crisis appears in the British newspapers to-day.

The more one considers the consequences which would follow from a decision which entailed the King's abdication, the more one realizes the sadness in which this country and the Dominions would be plunged, says the "Daily Telegraph."

The King has a magnetic quality of personal leadership, and the Dominions and India have been eagerly looking forward to welcoming him once more among them, this time as their Sovereign. If the whole programme had to be changed, the adjusting task would everywhere be undertaken with great reluctance.

"We are convinced," the "Daily Telegraph" continues, "that the general feeling throughout the Empire will be one of profound relief and thankfulness if the King's decision proves to be in accordance with the general desire, while the King's Ministers, who have felt bound by their sense of moral and political duty to refuse his request, will rejoice most of all."

The "Daily Mail" says that Mrs. Simpson's proferred abandonment of "any action or proposal that would hurt or damage His Majesty or the Throne" changes the whole position. It opens hope for a speedy end to this grave, disquieting crisis.

Mrs. Simpson, the journal adds, renders it possible for the King to continue upon the Throne, and thus relieve the country and the Empire of the heart-breaking loss which his abdication would involve.

"We can rejoice," says the "Daily Express," "The crisis has passed into history, and the King is still with us. No question of the Crown overriding the Cabinet has arisen, nor have the Ministers imposed surrender upon the King on this highly personal issue."

Advice Of Ministers

"The Times," in a leader, declares that the King has proposed a certain course of action and has been advised, in constitutional form, that it is impracticable. There is no reason to doubt that he has accepted this advice.

In extreme cases where the Sovereign doubts the authority of public opinion behind his Ministers and Parliament, the Constitution provides him with means to appeal, but this is clearly not such a case, and there is no indication that His Majesty supposes it to be so.

The plan for a morganatic marriage has, therefore, been abandoned, adds "The Times," and what the King has been considering is whether to take any other form of action.

For His Majesty to take no action, "The Times" declares, is to acquiesce in the failure of what is known to be his heart's desire, but, on the other hand, no positive action has been suggested except one from which the whole Empire shrinks.

To urge the second alternative by direct or indirect persuasion is a course that no constitutional Cabinet could have any excuse for taking, and it has not been done.

All a minister can do is to answer such questions as the King may put to him in order that His Majesty may have the fullest possible understanding of the nature of the consequences of any action that he may choose to take.—Reuter.

Rumours Regarding Danish Estate

COPENHAGEN, Dec. 9.—Sir Charles Lampe, chamberlain to King Edward VIII, during the course of a trip here last week visited many estates that were for sale, the "Social Demokraten" reports.

The journal suggests that the King might contemplate settling in Denmark in case of abdication.—Havas.

《字林西报》，1936年12月10日，星期四

等待国王决定

国王退位将是重大打击

英国及各自治领将陷入深切悲痛

陛下之个人领导魅力

英国报界相信危机最糟糕的阶段已过

伦敦，12月9日。— 英国报纸今天进一步评论宪政危机。

《每日电讯报》称，人们越是考虑国王退位这一决定所带来的后果，就越能意识到这个国家和各自治领将陷入何种悲痛之中。

国王具有磁石般的个人领导魅力，各自治领和印度一直热切期盼再次欢迎他来到他们中间，这次是以君主的身份。如果整个计划必须改变，各地的调整工作都将极不情愿地进行。

《每日电讯报》继续说道：“我们确信，如果国王的决定符合普遍愿望，整个帝国的情绪将是深深的宽慰和感激，而因道德和政治责任感而不得不拒绝国王请求的大臣们，将最为高兴。”

《每日邮报》称，辛普森夫人主动放弃“任何会伤害或损害陛下或王位的行动或提议”，改变了整个局面。这为迅速结束这场严重且令人不安的危机带来了希望。

该报补充说，辛普森夫人使国王得以继续留在王位上，从而使国家和帝国免于因他退位而带来的令人心碎的损失。

《每日快报》称：“我们可以庆幸，危机已成为历史，国王仍与我们在一起。没有出现王权凌驾于内阁之上的问题，大臣们也没有在这个高度个人化的问题上强迫国王屈服。”

大臣们的建议

《泰晤士报》在一篇社论中宣称，国王提出了某种行动方案，并依宪政形式被告知该方案不可行。没有理由怀疑他没有接受这一建议。

在君主怀疑其大臣和议会背后的公众舆论权威性的极端情况下，宪法为他提供了上诉的手段，但这显然不属于此类情况，也没有迹象表明陛下认为属于此类情况。

《泰晤士报》补充说，贵贱通婚的计划因此已被放弃，国王一直在考虑的是是否采取其他形式的行动。

《泰晤士报》宣称，陛下若不采取行动，即是默许已知为其心中所愿之事失败；但另一方面，除了整个帝国都畏缩不前的那种行动外，并未提出任何积极的行动建议。

通过直接或间接的劝说来敦促第二种选择，是任何宪政内阁都没有借口采取的行动方针，而且事实上也未这样做。

大臣所能做的，就是回答国王可能向他提出的任何问题，以便陛下能够尽可能充分地理解他选择采取的任何行动的后果性质。— 路透社。

关于丹麦地产的谣言

哥本哈根，12月9日。— 《社会民主党人报》报道，爱德华八世国王的侍从长查尔斯·兰佩爵士上周在此旅行期间，参观了许多待售的地产。

该报暗示，国王可能在退位的情况下考虑定居丹麦。— 哈瓦斯社。

BROTHER COMMENDED TO NATION

"I am deeply sensible of the consideration which they have always extended to me both before and after my accession to the Throne, and which I know they will extend in full measure to my successor.

"I am most anxious that there should be no delay in giving effect to the Instrument which I have executed, and that all the necessary steps should be taken immediately to secure that my lawful successor, my brother, His Royal Highness the Duke of York, should ascend the Throne."

TENSE, PACKED HOUSE

The scene in the House was illuminated by the mellow light of electric lamps, which had been turned on because the fog outside blanketed the daylight.

Never has the House been so full as it was to-day.

All the benches were packed when the session was opened with the exception of the places of Mr. Baldwin, Mr. C. R. Attlee, leader of the Labour Opposition, and Sir Archibald Sinclair, the Liberal leader, who all arrived later.

The Peers, Diplomatic and Dominion galleries were likewise full, and many persons were unable to obtain admission.

Fifty questions were asked and quickly answered, most of them inaudible amid the excited hum of a tense audience. Members heard the questions listlessly and impatiently, restively awaiting Mr. Baldwin's announcement.

Historic Occasion

All were obviously conscious of the gravity of the most historic parliamentary occasion since the outbreak of the Great War.

As the murky daylight of a foggy December day faded, the lights in the House were switched on, throwing into greater relief the sombreness of the scene.

Nearly everyone, including women, wore black, which matched the sadness of their thoughts.

Mr. Baldwin arrived at 3.35 p.m., and was greeted with a restrained, but wholehearted cheer.

The Prime Minister sat forward uneasily in his chair, shuffling papers in his hand and whispering with Mr. Ramsay MacDonald, Lord President of the Council, and the Home Secretary, Sir John Simon, who sat on either side of him.

Mr. Baldwin was very pale. He wore a short black coat, striped trousers and a black tie.

Questions terminated at 3.30 p.m. and, at 3.42 p.m., Mr. Baldwin rose, slowly walked to the Bar of the House and announced that he had a message from King Edward signed in his own hand.

He then handed the message to the Speaker, who read it out in a grave voice.

PREMIER'S STATEMENT

After King Edward's message had been read, Mr. Baldwin made a statement.

"I have to move," he said, "that His Majesty's most gracious message be now considered.

"No graver message has ever been received by Parliament, and no more difficult—I may almost say repugnant—task has ever been imposed upon a Prime Minister.—(Cheers).

"I would ask the House, which I know will not be without sympathy for me in my position today—(renewed sympathetic cheers)—to remember that in this last week I have had but little time in which to compose a speech for delivery, so I must tell what I have to tell truthfully, sincerely and plainly, with no attempt to dress up or at adornment.

No Praise Or Blame

"I shall have little or nothing to say in the way of comment, or any criticism or praise or blame.

"I think my best course is to tell, so far as I can, what has passed between His Majesty and myself and what has led up to the present situation.

"I would like to say, at the start, that His Majesty, as Prince of Wales, honoured me for many years with a friendship which I value.

"I know he would agree with me in saying to you that it was not only a friendship between man and man, but friendship and affection.

Friendship Unimpaired

"I would like to tell the House that when we said good-bye on Tuesday night at Fort Belvedere we both felt, and said to each other, that our friendship had so far been unimpaired, and that our discussions in these last few weeks had bound us more closely together than they ever did, and would last for life.—(Cheers).

First Interview With King

Describing how he had his first interview with King Edward, Mr. Baldwin said that after his own holiday in October he had been disquieted by the vast volume of correspondence coming in from British subjects in America, and also from the Dominions, expressing perturbation over what was appearing in the American press.

He was also aware that a divorce case was approaching the results of which threatened a difficult situation. Without consulting his colleagues, he saw the King privately on October 20 and spoke to him of the difficult situation that would arise if gossip and criticism continued.

"The King's attitude throughout," Mr. Baldwin continued, "has been such that he has never shown a sign of offence or hurt at anything I said to him."

He reminded the King that, while the British Crown had been deprived of many prerogatives through the centuries, it stood to-day for far more than ever in history—(cheers)—and once respect for the Crown was lost he doubted whether anything would ever restore it.

He repeatedly told the King "You and I must settle this matter together," and pointed out the dangers of the divorce proceeding.

Second Admonition

Mr. Baldwin next saw the King on November 16, after the decree nisi had been pronounced, and told him that a particular marriage would not receive the approbation of the country.

"The King," Mr. Baldwin proceeded, "said he had been wanting to tell me something for a long time, namely: 'I am going to marry Mrs. Simpson, and I am prepared to go'."

Meanwhile a compromise was suggested—that Parliament pass an Act enabling the lady to be the King's wife without the position of Queen.

He, Mr. Baldwin, had expressed the opinion that Parliament would never pass such legislation, but had told the King that he would consult the Cabinet.

Enquiries showed that there was no prospect of such legislation being accepted by Great Britain and the Dominions. When informed of this, the King was not surprised, and did not refer to the matter again.

Behaved Like A Gentleman

"He behaved," said Mr. Baldwin, "as a gentleman," and insisted that he would not allow a situation to arise in which he could not go with dignity. The idea of a so-called "King's Party" was abhorrent to His Majesty.—(Loud cheers.)

Mr. Baldwin read a pencilled note received from King Edward this morning stating that he was confident the Duke of York deserved and would receive the support of the whole Empire.—(Loud cheers).

The Prime Minister emphasised that his efforts in the past days had been directed towards trying to help the King make a choice which he had not made.

Yesterday morning, when the King had made a final decision, the Cabinet unanimously appealed to him to reconsider a step which would cause deep distress to his subjects. The King regretted that he was unable to alter his decision.

Mr. Baldwin's voice sank to a whisper at the conclusion of his speech. "Let us," he said, "conduct ourselves with the dignity which the King is showing, and let us rally behind the new King."—(Prolonged cheers).

Bill Of Abdication

After a brief, sympathetic statement by Mr. C. R. Attlee, the House adjourned till 6 o'clock this afternoon for consideration of a Bill of Abdication.

This will pass the remaining stages in both Houses to-morrow, and King Edward will sign the Abdication Act to-morrow night.

The Accession Council will meet on Saturday morning, and the new King will be proclaimed on Saturday afternoon.

All the Dominions except the Irish Free State have agreed to the enactment of the necessary legislation.

Mr. Eamon de Valera, president of the Executive Council, announced to-day that the Dail would meet to-morrow, as the question affected the Irish Free State.—Reuter.

OVATION FOR PREMIER

LONDON, Dec. 10.—Police cleared Downing Street as the time approached for the Prime Minister, Mr. Stanley Baldwin, to leave No. 10, his official residence, to make his momentous statement in the House of Commons on King Edward's abdication.

An army of cameramen took photographs of Mr. Baldwin as he left.

The first people to see him led an outburst of cheering which increased into a great ovation as his car progressed to Parliament. Men waved their hats and women furried their handkerchiefs.

There were one or two outbursts of booing, but these were swamped in the roars of cheers.

The crowd was so great outside Buckingham Palace that the roadway became impassable, and police reinforcements had to be called up to keep people on the move.

Queen Mary was given loud cheers on her arrival at the Duke of York's house in Piccadilly at 3 o'clock this afternoon.

1/G13

国王之弟获举国赞誉

“我深切感受到他们在我即位前后始终给予我的体谅，我也知道他们会以同样的充分程度将这份体谅给予我的继任者。

“我迫切希望我所签署的文件能立即生效，并立即采取一切必要步骤，确保我的合法继承人、我的弟弟约克公爵殿下（His Royal Highness the Duke of York）登基。”

气氛紧张，座无虚席

议会大厅内的场景被电灯柔和的光线照亮，这是因为外面的大雾遮蔽了日光。

下议院从未像今天这样满员。

会议开始时，除了鲍德温先生（Mr. Baldwin）、工党反对派领袖艾德礼先生（Mr. C. R. Attlee）和自由党领袖辛克莱爵士（Sir Archibald Sinclair）的席位外，所有长椅都坐满了人，他们随后才到达。

贵族旁听席、外交使团旁听席和自治领旁听席也同样爆满，许多人无法进入。

五十个问题被提出并迅速得到回答，在紧张的听众激动的嗡嗡声中，大多数回答都听不清楚。议员们无精打采且不耐烦地听着这些问题，焦躁不安地等待着鲍德温先生的宣布。

历史性时刻

所有人都明显意识到，这是自大战爆发以来最具历史意义的议会时刻，其严肃性不言而喻。

随着十二月雾天昏暗的日光逐渐消逝，下议院内的灯光亮起，使现场阴郁的气氛更加突出。

几乎所有人，包括女性，都身着黑衣，这与他们悲伤的心绪相契合。

鲍德温先生于下午3点35分抵达，受到克制但衷心的欢呼欢迎。

首相不安地坐在椅子前沿，手里整理着文件，并与坐在他两侧的枢密院院长拉姆齐·麦克唐纳先生（Mr. Ramsay MacDonald）和内政大臣约翰·西蒙爵士（Sir John Simon）低声交谈。

鲍德温先生脸色非常苍白。他身穿黑色短外套、条纹长裤，系着黑色领带。

提问环节于下午3点30分结束，下午3点42分，鲍德温先生起身，缓缓走到下议院围栏处（Bar of the House），宣布他带来了一份由爱德华国王亲笔签名的讯息。

随后他将讯息交给议长，议长以庄严的声音宣读了该讯息。

首相声明

在爱德华国王的讯息宣读完毕后，鲍德温先生发表声明。

他说：“我必须动议，现在审议陛下最仁慈的讯息。

“议会从未收到过比这更严重的讯息，也从未有一项任务像这样艰难——我几乎可以说是令人反感——强加于首相身上。（欢呼声）。

“我请求下议院，我知道诸位对我今天的处境并非没有同情心（再次响起同情的欢呼声），请记住，在过去的一周里，我几乎没有时间来构思一篇演讲，所以我必须真实、诚恳且直白地陈述我要说的话，不试图粉饰或修饰。

不予褒贬

“我将很少或根本不发表评论，也不进行任何批评、赞扬或指责。

“我认为我最好的做法是尽可能如实告知陛下与我之间发生的事情，以及导致目前局势的原因。

“我想首先说明，陛下在作为威尔士亲王期间，多年来一直惠赐我友谊，对此我珍视有加。

“我知道他会同意我对你们说，这不仅是人与人之间的友谊，更是友情与 affection（情谊/爱戴）。

友谊未损

“我想告诉下议院，当我们周二晚上在贝尔维德雷堡（Fort Belvedere）道别时，我们都感到并相互表示，我们的友谊至今未受损害，而且过去几周的讨论使我们比以往任何时候都结合得更紧密，并将持续终生。（欢呼声）。

首次觐见国王

在描述他如何首次会见爱德华国王时，鲍德温先生说，他在十月份休假结束后，对来自美国以及自治领的英国臣民的大量来信感到不安，这些信件表达了对美国报纸报道内容的忧虑。

他也意识到一桩离婚案即将宣判，其结果可能引发困难局面。在未咨询同僚的情况下，他于10月20日私下会见了国王，并向他谈到如果流言蜚语和批评继续下去将会出现的困难局面。

鲍德温先生继续说道：“国王在整个过程中的态度是，对于我对他说的任何话，他从未表现出丝毫的冒犯或受伤。”

他提醒国王，虽然英国王冠在几个世纪中被剥夺了许多特权，但它今天所代表的意义远超历史上任何时期——（欢呼声）——一旦失去对王冠的尊重，他怀疑是否还有什么能将其恢复。

他反复告诉国王：“你和我必须共同解决这件事”，并指出了离婚诉讼的危险。

第二次劝诫

鲍德温先生随后于11月16日再次会见国王，当时临时判决令（decree nisi）已颁布，他告诉国王，特定的婚姻不会得到国家的认可。

鲍德温先生接着说：“国王说他很久以来就想告诉我一件事，即：‘我要娶辛普森夫人（Mrs. Simpson），我准备离开’。”

与此同时，有人提出了一项妥协方案——即议会通过一项法案，使该女士成为国王的妻子，但不拥有王后的地位。

他，鲍德温先生，曾表示意见认为议会永远不会通过此类立法，但他告诉国王他将咨询内阁。

调查显示，英国和自治领接受此类立法的可能性为零。当得知这一情况时，国王并不惊讶，也没有再提及此事。

举止如绅士

鲍德温先生说：“他的举止像一位绅士，”并坚持认为他不会允许出现使他无法体面行事的情况。所谓“国王派”的想法令陛下深恶痛绝。（热烈欢呼。）

鲍德温先生宣读了今天早上收到的爱德华国王用铅笔写的一张便条，上面 stating（写明）他确信约克公爵值得并会得到整个帝国的支持。（热烈欢呼）。

首相强调，他在过去几天的努力旨在帮助国王做出一个他尚未做出的选择。

昨天早上，当国王做出最终决定时，内阁一致呼吁他重新考虑这一步骤，因为这会给他的臣民带来深深的痛苦。国王遗憾地表示他无法改变决定。

鲍德温先生在演讲结束时声音降低为耳语。他说：“让我们以国王所展现的尊严来行事，让我们团结在新国王身后。”（长时间的欢呼）。

退位法案

在艾德礼先生（Mr. C. R. Attlee）发表简短而同情的声明后，下议院休会至今天下午6点，以审议《退位法案》。

该法案将于明天在两院通过剩余阶段，爱德华国王将于明晚签署《退位法》。

继位委员会将于周六上午召开会议，新国王将于周六下午 proclamation（宣告即位）。

除爱尔兰自由邦外，所有自治领均已同意制定必要的立法。

行政委员会主席埃蒙·德·瓦莱拉先生（Mr. Eamon de Valera）今天宣布，由于该问题涉及爱尔兰自由邦，达伊尔（Dail，爱尔兰议会）将于明天开会。——路透社。

为首相喝彩

伦敦，12月10日。——随着首相斯坦利·鲍德温先生（Mr. Stanley Baldwin）离开其官邸唐宁街10号，前往下议院就爱德华国王退位一事发表重大声明的时间临近，警察清空了唐宁街。

一大群摄影师在鲍德温先生离开时拍摄了他的照片。

第一批看到他的人引发了一阵欢呼，随着他的汽车驶向议会，欢呼声演变成巨大的喝彩。男人们挥舞帽子，女人们挥动手帕。

虽然有一两阵嘘声，但这些声音被欢呼的 roar（轰鸣声）所淹没。

白金汉宫外面的人群如此之多，以至于道路变得无法通行，不得不调用增援警力来维持人群流动。

玛丽王后（Queen Mary）今天下午3点抵达皮卡迪利（Piccadilly）的约克公爵府邸时，受到了热烈的欢呼。

Tension In Whitehall
An atmosphere of acute tension
prevailed in Whitehall all day to-
day.
The Speaker, Captain E. A.
Fitzroy, took his seat in the House
of Commons at 2.45 p.m., and Mr.
Baldwin began his momentous an-
nouncement after questions had
been disposed of.
There was a constant stream of
telegraph and departmental mes-
sages this morning to No. 10
Downing Street, where crowds
gathered. Newspaper vendors had an
exceptionally busy day, every edi-
tion being snapped up by an eager
public anxious to learn the latest de-
velopments.
The anxiety of the people was
reflected in the faces of the King's
brothers, the Dukes of York,
Gloucester and Kent, who, all look-
ing pale, arrived separately at
Fort Belvedere at about 9.45 this
morning, each driving his own car.
Early this morning two motor-
cycle despatch riders arrived at
Fort Belvedere from No. 10
Downing Street bearing sealed cases
believed to contain important docu-
ments for King Edward. They had
left Downing Street an hour before,
when members of Mr. Baldwin's
staff assisted one of them to secure
to his machine a black tin box, to
which was affixed a great red seal.
Mr. Walter Mockton, K.C., At-
torney-General to the Duchy of
Cornwall, and Sir Edward Peacock,
Receiver-General to the Duchy, left
Fort Belvedere for London at 10.20
a.m.
Sir John Simon, the Home
Secretary, arrived at No. 10 Downing
Street at 10.35 this morning, followed
soon afterwards by Mr. Malcolm
MacDonald, Secretary of State for
the Dominions.
Last-Minute Conferences
Later Sir John motored to Fort
Belvedere, being the only member
of the Cabinet, apart from Mr.
Baldwin, to see the King since the
crisis developed.
The morning was characterized
by hectic last-moment conferences
and hasty comings and goings in
which Mr. Baldwin, Sir John Simon,
Mr. Malcolm MacDonald, Mr.
Monckton and Sir Edward Peacock
were prominent.
Public reaction, on the other
hand, was almost invisible despite
the shock caused by the sudden
change in the situation last night
which the morning newspapers
interpreted as meaning inevitable
abdication.
Large contingents of police were
brought to Westminster early in
the morning from outlying divi-
sions as a precautionary measure
to deal with any crowds which may
have endeavoured to congregate
near the House of Commons.
Police Precautions
The police precautions in the
region of Scotland Yard appeared
disproportionate to the probable
needs. Buses with reinforcements
from the suburbs disgorged foot
and mounted police, and vans
equipped with loud-speakers were
lined up.
Activity in Whitehall over the
crisis continued late into Wednes-
day night.
All the lights on the ground floor
at No. 10 Downing Street were still
burning at 2 a.m. to-day when a
member of Mr. Baldwin's staff,
bearing a sheaf of documents, cross-
ed to the Colonial Office.
Long after midnight messengers
were constantly going to and from
the Colonial Office, where Sir
Thomas Inskip, Minister for the
Co-ordination Defence, who is one
of the Government's chief legal
advisers, remained until eight
minutes past two.—Reuter.

白厅的紧张气氛

今天一整天，白厅弥漫着极度紧张的气氛。

议长菲茨罗伊上校（Captain E. A. Fitzroy）于下午2点45分在下议院就座，鲍德温先生在处理完提问后开始了他的重大宣布。

今天上午，电报和各部委的信使络绎不绝地送往唐宁街10号，那里聚集了人群。报贩度过了异常忙碌的一天，每一版报纸都被渴望了解最新进展的热切公众抢购一空。

民众的焦虑反映在国王的兄弟们——约克公爵、格洛斯特公爵（Duke of Gloucester）和肯特公爵（Duke of Kent）的脸上，他们看起来都很苍白，于今天上午9点45分左右分别驾驶自己的汽车抵达贝尔维德雷堡。

今天清晨，两名摩托车信使从唐宁街10号抵达贝尔维德雷堡，携带着密封箱，据信里面装有给爱德华国王的重要文件。他们在一小时前离开唐宁街，当时鲍德温先生的一名工作人员协助其中一人将一个黑色锡盒固定在他的机器上，盒子上贴有一个巨大的红色封蜡。

康沃尔公国（Duchy of Cornwall）总检察长沃尔特·莫克顿先生（Mr. Walter Mockton, K.C.）和康沃尔公国总收税官爱德华·皮科克爵士（Sir Edward Peacock）于上午10点20分离开贝尔维德雷堡前往伦敦。

内政大臣约翰·西蒙爵士（Sir John Simon）于今天上午10点35分抵达唐宁街10号，紧随其后的是自治领事务大臣马尔科姆·麦克唐纳先生（Mr. Malcolm MacDonald）。

最后时刻的会议

后来，约翰爵士乘车前往贝尔维德雷堡，他是除鲍德温先生外，自危机爆发以来唯一会见国王的内阁成员。

上午的特点是混乱的最后时刻会议和匆忙的来来往往，鲍德温先生、约翰·西蒙爵士、马尔科姆·麦克唐纳先生、蒙克顿先生（Mr. Monckton）和爱德华·皮科克爵士在其中扮演了重要角色。

另一方面，尽管昨晚局势的突然变化引起了震惊，晨报将其解读为意味着不可避免的退位，但公众的反应几乎不可见。

作为预防措施，大批警察清晨从外围分区被调往威斯敏斯特，以应对任何可能试图在下议院附近聚集的人群。

警方预防措施

苏格兰场（Scotland Yard）地区的警方预防措施似乎与可能的需求不成比例。载有来自郊区增援部队的巴士卸下了徒步和骑警，配备扬声器的货车排成一列。

白厅围绕危机的活动一直持续到周三深夜。

今天凌晨2点，唐宁街10号一楼的所有灯光仍然亮着，当时鲍德温先生的一名工作人员抱着一叠文件穿过马路前往殖民部。

午夜过后很久，信使仍在殖民部进进出出，负责协调国防的大臣托马斯·因斯基普爵士（Sir Thomas Inskip）——他是政府的主要法律顾问之一——一直留在那里直到两点零八分。——路透社。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 11, 1936    1-912

Personal Message Read
Before Crowded House
Of Commons Yesterday

FINAL AND IRREVOCABLE DECISION IS
ANNOUNCED IN POIGNANT PLEA FOR
HIS PEOPLE'S UNDERSTANDING

CAN NO LONGER DISCHARGE HEAVY TASK
WITH EFFICIENCY OR SATISFACTION

Duke Of York Named As Successor By King, Who
Commends Him To Nation; Most Historic
Parliamentary Occasion In Decades

LONDON, Dec. 10.—King Edward VIII announced his abdication in a message read to the House of Commons this afternoon. He is to renounce all his titles and become plain “Mr. Windsor.” Possibly he will receive a Dukedom later.

He is succeeded by his brother, the Duke of York, who, although he was formerly known as Prince Albert, may choose the title of George VI, taking the last of his four names.

So ended the constitutional crisis which last week plunged the British Empire into doubt and suspense.

The King’s message, which was read by the Speaker, Mr. E. A. Fitzroy, in an atmosphere of the utmost tension, was:—

“After long and anxious consideration, I am determined to renounce the Throne to which I succeeded on the death of my father, and I am now communicating this my final, irrevocable decision.

“Realizing as I do the gravity of this step, I can only hope that I shall have the understanding of my peoples in the decision I have taken and the reasons which have led me to take it.

“I will not enter now into my private feelings, but I would beg that it should be remembered that the burden which constantly rests upon the shoulders of a sovereign is so heavy that it can only be borne in circumstances different from those in which I now find myself.

“I AM NOT OVERLOOKING DUTY”

“I conceive that I am not overlooking the duty that rests on me to place in the forefront the public interests when I declared that I am conscious that I can no longer discharge this heavy task with efficiency or with satisfaction to myself.

“I have accordingly this morning executed an Instrument of Abdication in the terms following:

‘I, Edward VIII, of Great Britain, Ireland and the British Dominions beyond the Seas King, Emperor of India, do hereby declare my irrevocable determination to renounce the Throne for myself and for my descendants, and my desire that effect should be given to this Instrument of Abdication immediately.

‘In token whereof I have hereunto set my hand this 10th day of December, 1936, in the presence of the witnesses, whose signatures are subscribed.’

(Signed) ‘EDWARD. R. I.’

“My execution of this Instrument has been witnessed by my three brothers, Their Royal Highnesses the Duke of York, the Duke of Gloucester and the Duke of Kent.

“MY MIND IS FULLY MADE UP”

“I deeply appreciate the spirit which has actuated the appeal which has been made to me to take a different decision, and I have, before reaching my final determination, most fully pondered over it, but my mind is fully made up.

“Moreover, further delay cannot but be most injurious to the peoples whom I have tried to serve as Prince of Wales and as King and whose future prosperity and happiness are the constant wish of my heart.

“I take my leave of them in the confident hope that the cause which I thought it right to follow is that which is best for the stability of the Throne and the Empire and the happiness of my peoples.”

昨日在下议院满座议员面前
宣读个人文告

在恳切呼吁国民理解的陈词中
宣布最终且不可撤销之决定

已无法高效或满意地
履行繁重职责

国王指定约克公爵为继任者，
并将其托付给国家；这是数十年来
最具历史意义的议会时刻

伦敦，12月10日电。——爱德华八世国王在今日下午向众议院宣读的文告中宣布退位。他将放弃所有头衔，成为普通的“温莎先生”。或许他日后会获封公爵爵位。

他的弟弟约克公爵将继承王位，尽管他此前被称为阿尔伯特亲王，但他可能会选择乔治六世作为尊号，取自其四个名字中的最后一个。

至此，上周令大英帝国陷入疑虑与悬而未决状态的宪政危机宣告结束。

议长E. A. 菲茨罗伊先生（Mr. E. A. Fitzroy）在极度紧张的气氛中宣读了国王的文告，内容如下：

“经过长期而焦虑的深思熟虑，我决心放弃在我父亲去世后即位的王位，现特此传达我这一最终且不可撤销的决定。

“我深知此举之严重性，唯愿我在作出此决定及其背后的原因时，能得到我国人民的谅解。

“此刻我不愿详述个人情感，但恳请铭记，君主肩上常负之重担如此沉重，唯有在不同于我当下所处之境况下，方能承担。

‘我并未忽视职责’

“当我宣称我意识到自己已无法高效或令自己满意地履行这一繁重任务时，我认为我并未忽视将公共利益置于首位的职责。

“因此，我已于今晨签署了一份退位诏书，条款如下：

‘我，大不列颠、爱尔兰及海外自治领国王，印度皇帝爱德华八世，在此声明我为自己及我的后代不可撤销地放弃王位的决心，并希望立即执行本退位诏书。

‘以此为证，我于1936年12月10日，在下列署名见证人在场的情况下，亲笔签署此文。’

（签名）‘爱德华。R. I.’

‘我的三位兄弟，即约克公爵、格洛斯特公爵和肯特公爵殿下，见证了我签署此诏书的过程。

‘我已下定决心’

‘对于促使我作出不同决定的呼吁中所体现的精神，我深表感激；在作出最终决定之前，我已对此进行了最充分的斟酌，但我已下定决心。

‘此外，进一步的拖延必将对那些我曾作为威尔士亲王及国王试图服务的人民造成极大伤害，他们的未来繁荣与幸福是我心中恒久的愿望。

‘我怀着坚定的希望向他们告别，我相信我所认为应当遵循的道路，最有利于王位与帝国的稳定以及我国人民的幸福。’”

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 12, 1936

Ex-King Boards Yacht At
Portsmouth Sailing For
Unknown Port In Secrecy

Utmost Precautions Taken To Prevent Knowledge
Of Destination Being Known; Definitely Not
Joining Mrs. Simpson In Cannes

POIGNANT FAREWELL TAKEN BY FORMER
MONARCH AMONG HIS FAMILY

LONDON, Dec. 12.—With the utmost secrecy ex-King Edward, now plain "Mr. Windsor," left the country for an unknown destination early to-day.

A few hours after giving his Assent to the Abdication Bill, his last act as monarch, he drove to Portsmouth, where he went aboard a British destroyer.

All was bustle and activity aboard the destroyer as luggage, which was carried by several cars, was rushed aboard. The ex-King was greeted on the pier by members of his suite. After taking farewells, he boarded the vessel, which shortly after moved away. Mr. Windsor had left England.

It is learned that "Mr. Windsor" is being accompanied on his voyage by his equerry, Lieut. Colonel Piers Legh, a personal detective and one member of his domestic staff.

The ex-King arrived at Portsmouth from Windsor about midnight in a motor car with the blinds drawn. Other cars, laden with luggage, followed. Members of his suite were waiting for him at the dock-yard.

Ex-King Is Duke
Of Windsor

LONDON, Dec. 12. — King George has conferred the first honour of his reign on his predecessor, who, on his abdication, gave up all his titles and became plain Edward Windsor, Esq.

His Majesty has made the ex-King "His Royal Highness the Duke of Windsor."

This means, of course, that when the former ruler marries Mrs. Ernest Simpson, the American lady for whom he relinquished the throne, she will become Duchess of Windsor.—Reuter.

Every member of the dock-yard staff was sworn to secrecy concerning the ex-King's movements and intentions.

The Wolfhound slipped alongside one of the jetties, where it was waiting with full steam up when the ex-King's car rushed through the dock-yard entrance.

Chatted To Admiral

The police on duty there evidently knew who was inside because they allowed it to pass the gates without hesitation.

The car proceeded immediately to the residence of Admiral Sir William Wordsworth Fisher, which is inside the dock-yard.

No one was allowed to follow the car in, but it is learned that the ex-King chatted for some time with Admiral Fisher before proceeding aboard the Enchantress.

The battleship Nelson could be seen in the distance with lights aglow, while the cruiser Neptune lay nearby.

All was bustle and activity aboard the Wolfhound as luggage was rushed aboard.

Farewell Family Party

Earlier in the evening a poignant farewell party was held at the Royal Lodge at Windsor, among those present besides the ex-King being his brother, the new King George VI, his mother, Queen Mary, the Duke of Gloucester, the Princess Royal, Princess Alice and the Earl of Athlone, uncle of the King.

A notable absentee was the new Queen Elizabeth, formerly Duchess of York, who has been confined to the house with a slight cold. It was considered inadvisable for her to go out in the cold night air.

Portsmouth was silent and deserted when the three cars of the ex-King swept through the gates of the dockyard, where no extra guards were on duty.

Later, another of the ex-King's cars, with a figure wrapped up in a large fawn coat seated behind the driver, drove through the main entrance to the dockyard.

The car was stopped by an officer at the gate, but after a whispered word it shot forward in the direction of the jetty.—Reuter.

Private Plane Leaves

LONDON, Dec. 12.—In connection with the departure of the ex-King his private plane left Hendon at 2.40 o'clock yesterday afternoon, piloted by Major Fielden, ex-King's pilot. The 'plane, which carried three passengers, whose identity was not disclosed, presumably proceeded to the private airfield near Fort Belvedere.

Earlier in the afternoon, the Tory leader, Mr. Winston Churchill, called at Fort Belvedere, spending several hours with the ex-Monarch, who was busy signing numerous documents, talking to the servants and giving last instructions in connection with his departure. The fate of the servants has not been settled yet. The detective who guarded the former King for many years, took leave of him yesterday.

Many persons called at the iron gates of Fort Belvedere, handing the Guard letters addressed personally to the ex-King. One of the messengers brought a prayer book and a huge bouquet of violets.

Well-informed quarters declare that the new King will most likely confer upon his brother the title of Duke of Sussex, or Albany.

Will Not Go To Cannes

Meanwhile, reports from Cannes confirmed that "Mr. David Windsor" as the ex-Monarch styled himself, will not go to Cannes, where his bride-to-be Mrs. Ernest Simpson, for whom he has given up the Throne, is now staying. It is stated that Mrs. Simpson will remain in Cannes for three or four more weeks, during which time she will not see the ex-King.

Rumours that a yacht was held ready in Monte Carlo to take on board the ex-King and Mrs. Simpson were authoritatively denied in Cannes. Mrs. Simpson is said to be in an excellent state of health, although slightly tired from the emotional strain of the past days. Yesterday afternoon she made an automobile journey to Grasse, a small town 25 miles distant from Nice.—Havas

Financial Position

LONDON, Dec. 12.—The former King, now Mr. "David Windsor," is left without an income, although the new King is likely to grant him a title, probably a dukedom with the revenue attached to it.

It will be recalled the late King George V left £4,000,000, but the former king is not entitled to any of it. The former king now owns only Fort Belvedere and the savings from the Duchy of Cornwall.—Havas.

"Defender Of The Faith"

LONDON, Dec. 12. — Much comment was raised here by the fact that the words "Defender of the Faith" figuring in the King's titles, did not figure in King Edward's message of abdication addressed to Parliament and read before the House of last Thursday.

Questioned yesterday in the House concerning the omission, the Home Secretary, Sir John Simon, said it did not appertain to Parliament to insert any alterations in the Act of Abdication.

The vagueness of Sir John's statement is generally interpreted here as meaning that the Home Secretary was anxious to avoid a debate on the omission which may have been an involuntary one.—Havas.

前国王在朴次茅斯登上游艇
秘密驶往未知港口

采取最高级别预防措施以防目的地泄露；
肯定未去戛纳与辛普森夫人会合

前君主与家人举行
感人的告别仪式

伦敦，12月12日电。——前国王爱德华，现为普通的“温莎先生”，于今日凌晨在极度保密的情况下离开本国，前往一个未知的目的地。

在签署《退位法案》使其生效——这是他作为君主的最后举动——数小时后，他驱车前往朴次茅斯，登上一艘英国驱逐舰。

随着几辆汽车运送的行李被匆忙搬上船，驱逐舰上一片忙碌景象。前国王在码头上受到其随从人员的迎接。告别之后，他登上船只，该船随后不久便驶离。温莎先生已离开英国。

据悉，“温莎先生”此次航行由他的侍从武官皮尔斯·莱中校（Lieut. Colonel Piers Legh）、一名私人侦探以及一名家仆陪同。

前国王于午夜时分乘坐一辆拉下窗帘的汽车从温莎抵达朴次茅斯。其他装载行李的车辆紧随其后。他的随从成员已在造船厂等候。

前国王受封
温莎公爵

伦敦，12月12日电。——乔治国王将其即位后的首项荣誉授予其前任，后者在退位时放弃了所有头衔，成为普通的爱德华·温莎绅士（Edward Windsor, Esq.）。

陛下已封前国王为“温莎公爵殿下”。

这意味着，当然，当前统治者迎娶那位令他放弃王位的美国女士欧内斯特·辛普森夫人（Mrs. Ernest Simpson）时，她将成为温莎公爵夫人。——路透社

造船厂的每一位员工都被勒令对前国王的行踪和意图保守秘密。

“猎狼犬”号（Wolfhound）悄悄靠上其中一个码头，当载有前国王的汽车冲过造船厂大门时，该船已蒸汽全开在此等候。

与海军上将交谈

那里的执勤警察显然知道车内是谁，因为他们毫不犹豫地放行通过大门。

汽车径直驶往位于造船厂内的威廉·沃兹沃思·费舍尔海军上将爵士（Admiral Sir William Wordsworth Fisher）的寓所。

无人被允许跟随车辆进入，但据悉前国王在与费舍尔海军上将交谈片刻后，才登上“ enchantress ”号（注：此处原文为Enchantress，通常译作“迷情女”号或音译，结合上下文应为其乘坐的游艇/船只名，前文提及驱逐舰，此处可能指代同一艘船或换乘，依原文保留或译为“恩昌特雷斯”号，鉴于历史事实为爱德华八世乘坐的是驱逐舰HMS Fury，后换乘游艇Nahlin，但档案原文写Enchantress，故按原文翻译为“恩昌特雷斯”号或保留英文，此处依指令保留原文加注音译或直译，考虑到是专有名词，译为“恩昌特雷斯”号）。

远处可见战列舰“纳尔逊”号灯火通明，巡洋舰“海王星”号停泊在附近。

随着行李被匆忙搬上船，“猎狼犬”号上一片忙碌景象。

家庭告别聚会

当晚早些时候，在温莎皇家别墅举行了一场感人的告别聚会，出席者除前国王外，还有他的弟弟、新国王乔治六世，其母玛丽王后，格洛斯特公爵，长公主，爱丽丝公主以及国王的舅舅阿思隆伯爵。

一位引人注目的缺席者是新任伊丽莎白王后，即前约克公爵夫人，她因患轻微感冒而居家休养。人们认为让她在寒冷的夜空中外出是不明智的。

当前国王的三辆汽车驶过造船厂大门时，朴次茅斯一片寂静，空无一人，那里没有增派警卫。

随后，前国王的另一辆汽车驶过造船厂正门，司机身后坐着一位裹在大件浅褐色大衣里的人。

汽车在门口被一名军官拦下，但在低声耳语一句后，便朝码头方向疾驰而去。——路透社

私人飞机起飞

伦敦，12月12日电。——与前国王离境相关，他的私人飞机于昨日下午2时40分从亨顿机场起飞，由前国王的飞行员菲尔登少校（Major Fielden）驾驶。这架载有三名身份未披露乘客的飞机，据推测飞往贝尔维德雷堡附近的私人机场。

当天下午早些时候，保守党领袖温斯顿·丘吉尔先生拜访了贝尔维德雷堡，与前君主共度数小时，当时后者正忙于签署大量文件、与仆人谈话并就其离境事宜发出最后指示。仆人们的去向尚未确定。守护前国王多年的侦探于昨日向他辞行。

许多人来到贝尔维德雷堡的铁门前，向卫兵递交写给前国王的私人信件。其中一名信使带来了一本祈祷书和一大束紫罗兰。

消息灵通人士称，新国王很可能会授予其弟弟苏塞克斯公爵或奥尔巴尼公爵的头衔。

不会前往戛纳

与此同时，来自戛纳的报道证实，自称为“大卫·温莎先生”的前君主不会前往戛纳，他为之放弃王位的未婚妻欧内斯特·辛普森夫人目前正住在那里。据说辛普森夫人将在戛纳再停留三至四周，在此期间她不会与前国王见面。

关于有一艘游艇在蒙特卡洛待命以接载前国王和辛普森夫人的谣言，在戛纳遭到权威方面的否认。据说辛普森夫人健康状况良好，尽管因过去几天的情绪压力而略显疲惫。昨日下午，她乘车前往格拉斯，这是一个距离尼斯25英里的小镇。——哈瓦斯社

财务状况

伦敦，12月12日电。——前国王，现为“大卫·温莎先生”，失去了收入来源，尽管新国王可能会授予他头衔，可能是附带收入的公爵爵位。

需指出的是，已故国王乔治五世留下了400万英镑，但前国王无权继承其中任何部分。前国王现在仅拥有贝尔维德雷堡以及来自康沃尔公国的储蓄。——哈瓦斯社

“信仰守护者”

伦敦，12月12日电。——国王头衔中出现的“信仰守护者”一词未出现在爱德华国王上周四向议会提交并在下议院宣读的退位文告中，这一事实在此地引发了诸多评论。

昨日在下议院就这一遗漏提出质询时，内政大臣约翰·西蒙爵士表示，议会无权在《退位法案》中插入任何修改。

约翰爵士声明的模糊性在此地普遍被解读为内政大臣急于避免就这一可能是无心的遗漏展开辩论。——哈瓦斯社
